sentences.text: InnerChange was a Utah-based company that owned residential treatment programs, mostly for adolescent girls and young women, from 2006 until 2018.
That year it was folded into Embark Behavioral Health.
It began as Solacium Holdings and was owned in turn by two private equity firms, CIC Partners and Cressey & Company.
Its record includes a New Haven therapist, Jason Scott Calder, who pleaded guilty in November 2017 to raping a 16-year-old patient.
The company took shape around two Utah treatment centers.
On July 1, 2006, New Haven, in Spanish Fork, bought Sunrise RTC, and both became part of Solacium Holdings, LLC.
In April 2007 Solacium merged with Wellcore, LLC, which owned Fulshear Ranch Academy in Texas.
That August Solacium, then based in Missouri City, Texas, signed a letter of intent to buy Wilderness Quest in Monticello, Utah.
Its chief executive, Val H. Christensen, announced that Alldredge Academy in West Virginia would drop its academic phase and become Alldredge Wilderness Journey.
In October 2007 Woodbury Reports listed Sommerville Young Adult Community, a program for young adults, as part of Solacium Holdings.
Whether the Wilderness Quest purchase closed is not on record; the company's December 2008 list of programs leaves it out.
By June 2008 CIC Partners of Dallas owned most of the company, which ran five programs.

Woodbury Reports announced that June that Anthony Geraci had resigned as Solacium's chief operations and marketing officer and that David Michel would succeed Christensen as president and chief executive.
In July 2008 Woodbury gave Solacium's address as Orem, Utah.
On November 3, 2008, its chief executive, David Michel, announced that Solacium was now InnerChange.
Its programs were New Haven, Sunrise, Fulshear Ranch Academy and Alldredge Wilderness Journey in West Virginia.
Alldredge Wilderness Journey closed in 2008.
In April 2009 Woodbury listed InnerChange's offices in Addison, Texas.
By July 2011 Dustin Tibbitts, New Haven's executive director, was also president of InnerChange.
In December 2011 Cressey & Company bought InnerChange from CIC Partners.
Under Cressey the company expanded.
In 2011 Lake House Academy in Flat Rock, North Carolina, told a court in a suit against its founder that it was in a prospective sale to InnerChange.

sources.cite: Lake House Academy v. Jennings (2011), court opinion

sentences.text: On January 2, 2013, it bought Chrysalis in Eureka, Montana, "the fourth facility to join the InnerChange family."
That August, describing itself as "a clinical and operational consulting organization," it began a partnership with the Oakley School in Oakley, Utah.
InnerChange also announced that Paul Taylor, the executive director of Copper Canyon Academy, would become Oakley's executive director.
The Oakley School announced in April 2017 that it would close, letting students stay until June 30.
In March 2016 Optimum Performance Institute, a residential treatment center in Southern California for people aged 17 to 28, joined.
In August 2018 Calo Programs bought Dragonfly Transitions, a program for young adults in Oregon, from Glen White and Mona Treadway.
Cressey & Company exited InnerChange that August.

sources.cite: Preqin, Cressey & Company investment record for InnerChange (exit August 2018)

sentences.text: In September 2017 the Utah County Sheriff's Office arrested Calder, a licensed therapist who had worked at New Haven.
Police said he sexually abused a 16-year-old patient during therapy sessions from March to June 2017.
Co-workers had noticed that his sessions with her ran late at night and included walks off the grounds, which he did not do with other patients.
He had been fired and was working at another treatment center in Salt Lake County.
In November 2017 he pleaded guilty to rape, object rape, forcible sodomy, forcible sexual abuse and obstructing justice.
In January 2018 he was sentenced to seven years to life in prison.
In October 2018 InnerChange, Calo Programs and two other companies took the shared name Embark Behavioral Health.
New Haven, Sunrise, Chrysalis, Optimum Performance Institute, Vive and Dragonfly Transitions went into Embark under InnerChange, and the name lived on as an Embark division.
Lake House Academy and Fulshear were listed under Calo.
Sunrise is still registered as Solacium Sunrise, LLC, after the company's first name.
After the merger, in April 2023, Oliver Whitcomb and Amy Clifford sued InnerChange Chrysalis, LLC and others in federal court in Montana, a personal-injury case.

sources.cite: Whitcomb et al. v. InnerChange Chrysalis, LLC et al., No. 9:23-cv-00039 (D. Mont.), docket

sentences.text: The suit alleged that a staff member sexually abused students and that other staff members knew of the abuse and allowed it to continue.

sources.cite: Whitcomb et al. v. InnerChange Chrysalis, LLC et al., No. 9:23-cv-00039 (D. Mont.), order, Oct 22, 2024

sentences.text: In December 2025 the parties agreed to dismiss it with prejudice; the docket records no judgment on the merits.

sources.cite: Whitcomb et al. v. InnerChange Chrysalis, LLC et al., No. 9:23-cv-00039 (D. Mont.), docket
